clauses.heading: Home Business > Definitions
clauses.text: “Home business” means a “business”, owned solely by an “insured” or by a partnership or joint venture made up solely of “insureds”, that is described as the home business in the Declarations, that is conducted primarily on the “residence premises”, that has no more than three “employees” at any one time, and that had gross annual revenue of no more than $250,000 in the year before the policy period.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Scope
clauses.text: This endorsement applies only to the “home business” described in the Declarations. Any other “business” of an “insured”, whether or not conducted on the “residence premises”, remains subject to all provisions of this policy concerning “business”, including the special limits of liability on “business” property and the business exclusion in Section II.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Section I > Other Structures
clauses.text: Paragraph 4 of Coverage B does not apply to a structure on the “residence premises” from which the “home business” is conducted, or in which property of the “home business” is stored.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Section I > Business Property
clauses.text: The special limits of liability for property used primarily for “business” purposes in Coverage C do not apply to property of the “home business”. Property of the “home business” on the “residence premises” is covered up to the Coverage C limit of liability. Property of the “home business” away from the “residence premises” is covered up to $5,000.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Section I > Inventory and Property of Others
clauses.text: Property of the “home business” held for sale or delivery after sale is covered up to $10,000 in any one loss. Property of customers in the care of an “insured” for the “home business” is covered up to $2,500 in any one loss. “Business” data remains not covered, except the cost to replace blank recording media.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Section I > Loss of Business Income
clauses.text: If a loss covered under Section I to the “residence premises” causes a necessary suspension of the “home business”, we will pay the actual loss of business income you sustain, and necessary extra expense, for up to 12 months after the date of loss. Business income means net income that would have been earned plus continuing normal operating expenses, including payroll.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Section II > Liability
clauses.text: The business exclusion in Section II does not apply to “bodily injury” or “property damage” arising out of the “home business”, including injury to customers and visitors on the “residence premises” and injury arising out of products the “home business” makes or sells. Coverage F applies to customers and visitors of the “home business” injured on the “insured location”.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Section II > Exclusions
clauses.text: With respect to the “home business”, Coverages E and F do not apply to “bodily injury” to an “employee” arising out of and in the course of employment; to “bodily injury” or “property damage” arising out of professional services; or to “bodily injury” or “property damage” arising out of “home business” activities conducted away from the “residence premises”, other than products the “home business” has sold.

clauses.heading: Home Business > Section II > Products Aggregate
clauses.text: The most we will pay for all “bodily injury” and “property damage” arising out of products the “home business” makes or sells, in the policy period, is an aggregate equal to the Coverage E limit of liability.
